status_definitions.verified: Canonical repository/source inspected and core description grounded in it.
status_definitions.rejected: Could not be substantiated or was materially misleading.

tools.name: OpenOSINT
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: Natural-language OSINT interface with modular tools and MCP support.

tools.name: Taranis AI
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: Collects OSINT content and uses NLP/AI enrichment within an analyst-oriented workflow.

tools.name: PANO
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: Investigation platform combining graph, timeline, map and PANAI assistant capabilities.

tools.name: Argus OS
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: Agentic OSINT orchestration platform with adapters and configurable model providers.

tools.name: osint-mcp-server
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: Exposes multiple OSINT and infrastructure intelligence sources through MCP.

tools.name: MCP DadosBR
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: MCP server connecting AI assistants to Brazilian public-data sources.

tools.name: Focal Harvest
tools.verification: README inspected
tools.notes: Research and OSINT collection pipeline with LLM synthesis and local statistical fallback.

tools.name: OSINTai
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected; current README identifies v4.2.0 and local-first Ollama architecture.
tools.notes: Asynchronous OSINT crawler with deterministic post-crawl analysis, evidence-labelled findings, correlations, timelines and graph export. A separate UberGuidoZ/osintai lineage mirrors related v4 material; provenance is documented separately.

tools.name: Robin
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected.
tools.notes: AI-assisted dark-web OSINT research tool with multi-model support, Streamlit UI, MCP support and grounded follow-up analysis. Cataloged for lawful investigative use; operational access instructions are intentionally not reproduced here.

tools.name: WorldView
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected.
tools.notes: Self-hosted tactical intelligence platform using CesiumJS, LangGraph, local vLLM inference, Qdrant and Neo4j with live aviation, maritime, satellite and earthquake feeds.

tools.name: FETIH
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected; claims of 20+ AI providers and 912+ skills are maintainer-reported as of review date.
tools.notes: Cybersecurity AI agent supporting OSINT among broader security workflows, with persistent memory, skills, desktop/terminal interfaces and local-model support.

tools.name: Unburden
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected; maintainer reports 84 integrated security tools including 61 OSINT tools.
tools.notes: Local-LLM security orchestration platform using Qwen via Ollama, LlamaIndex and multiple MCP servers. OSINT capabilities are cataloged separately from its broader penetration-testing features.

tools.name: Banshee-AI
tools.verification: Canonical repository README and Go module metadata inspected.
tools.notes: Go-based AI-assisted search and OSINT CLI that generates and refines search queries, organizes findings and supports repeatable authorized discovery workflows.

tools.name: OWASP Social OSINT Agent
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected.
tools.notes: Autonomous social-media OSINT agent with text and vision analysis, cross-platform collection, evidence-linked media analysis, offline cached-analysis mode and indirect prompt-injection mitigations.

tools.name: GreyNoise MCP Server
tools.verification: Official GreyNoise repository and documentation inspected.
tools.notes: Official MCP server exposing GreyNoise threat-intelligence capabilities including IP context, GNQL, tags, CVEs, temporal analysis and entitlement-dependent operational actions.

tools.name: Theosight
tools.verification: Official Eos Applications product page inspected.
tools.notes: Commercial military-OSINT platform emphasizing structured intelligence, per-field provenance, NATO-oriented schemas and sovereign/on-prem deployment. The earlier claim that launch is planned for 2027 was not retained because the product is already presented publicly as an active offering.

tools.name: Argus — Local-First OSINT Framework
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected. Zero-cloud/local Ollama design verified. Module count is internally inconsistent: README headline says 13 while the current module table enumerates 14 entries.
tools.notes: Distinct from AXRoux/argus-os. Designed around local inference and mostly keyless/free sources. Exact module count should not be repeated without re-checking the current README.

tools.name: osint-mcp
tools.verification: Canonical GitHub repository and PyPI package inspected; both currently document 26 wrapped OSINT tools and 15 tools usable without an API key.
tools.notes: Python MCP package that wraps existing OSINT utilities behind a single MCP server. Active operations remain distinct from passive collection and require operator authorization.

tools.name: IntelHub
tools.verification: Mozilla Add-ons listing and version history inspected; v5.0.2 documents a Local OSINT Agent powered through LM Studio.
tools.notes: Firefox OSINT extension with local AI chat, local metadata/hash processing and web-search integration. 'No data leaves your machine' applies to local model/chat processing, while live web search necessarily makes network requests.

tools.name: Deep Research Investigator (DRI)
tools.verification: Official S2W Decision AI and XARVIS product pages inspected.
tools.notes: Domain-specific investigation agent deployed in XARVIS, linking search, graph analysis and profiling to support investigators. Treated as decision support, not as evidence by itself.

tools.name: AIL Framework
tools.verification: Canonical AIL repository and official AIL documentation inspected.
tools.notes: CIRCL-originated framework for collecting and analyzing unstructured data from web, Tor, I2P, chats, files and feeds. Supports OCR, QR/barcode extraction, correlation, MISP integration and AI-assisted image descriptions; official FAQ documents Qwen2.5-VL for image description.

tools.name: ShadowBroker / InfoNet
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected; InfoNet is explicitly documented as an experimental testnet with no current privacy guarantee.
tools.notes: Aggregates public intelligence feeds and includes the experimental InfoNet decentralized intelligence mesh. Privacy primitives are incomplete; the project itself warns users to treat current channels as public.

tools.name: The Big Brother
tools.verification: Canonical repository README inspected. Current public version is V7.0 (NEXUS), not V6.0.
tools.notes: Broad OSINT/threat-intelligence suite whose current maintainer documentation advertises 52 engines across 26 tabs. Some capabilities extend beyond passive OSINT into active security testing, so OSINTAI classifies it as dual-use rather than treating all modules as ordinary OSINT.

tools.name: NovBase-VTX
tools.verification: Public Hugging Face organization page inspected; core implementation is explicitly private and no public model code is available for independent review.
tools.notes: Maintainer describes a five-layer cognitive OSINT architecture with eight parallel units and local synthesis. Treated as a candidate research project because architecture and performance claims cannot yet be independently audited.

tools.name: Starcom
tools.verification: Official Starcom/Archangel Initiative pages inspected. The project page explicitly states the platform is still developing and not yet a fully operational MVP.
tools.notes: Experimental decentralized intelligence concept combining 3D visualization, OSINT workflows and decentralized infrastructure. Claims around tokenized intelligence and post-quantum features require feature-level verification before promotion.
